senses.definition: to include something as a necessary part, concern someone, or make them take part
senses.example: The project involves working with children.

senses.definition: the act of protecting someone or something, or an argument supporting a person or idea
senses.example: The team played well in defense.
senses.note: 美式拼写 defense；英式通常写 defence。

senses.definition: the way a person, animal, or thing acts
senses.example: The teacher praised the child's kind behavior.
senses.note: 美式拼写 behavior；英式通常写 behaviour。

senses.definition: any person, especially in questions, negatives, or statements without a particular person in mind
senses.example: Does anyone know the answer?

senses.definition: to become larger or make something larger in amount or number
senses.example: The company increased its prices last year.

senses.definition: a rise in an amount, number, or level
senses.example: There was an increase in sales.

senses.definition: a state of being safe, actions that keep people safe, or property promised for a loan
senses.example: The building has strict security at night.

senses.definition: used when the speaker is also the person affected by an action, or to emphasize who did it
senses.example: I made this cake myself.

senses.zh: 银行；河岸；堤岸；一排（机器）
senses.definition: a place that handles money, the land beside a river, or a row of similar objects
senses.example: The path runs along the river bank.

senses.zh: 存入银行；积存；使倾斜飞行
senses.definition: to put money in a bank, save something for later, or turn an aircraft by tilting
senses.example: She banks part of her pay each month.

senses.definition: used to show that something is sure, or to give a polite strong agreement
senses.example: Certainly, I can help you with that.

senses.definition: the direction where the sun sets, or the western part of a place
senses.example: The storm came from the west.

senses.definition: located towards the western part of a place
senses.example: They live on the west side of town.

senses.definition: towards or in the western direction
senses.example: We drove west all morning.

senses.zh: 体育运动；运动项目；消遣
senses.definition: physical games and competitions, or an activity done for enjoyment
senses.example: Football is a popular sport.

senses.definition: to wear or display something in a noticeable way
senses.example: He sported a bright red jacket.
senses.note: 动词 sport 多用于描述外表，和“做运动”不同。

senses.definition: a flat piece of wood, a group that manages an organization, a flat surface for an activity, or meals provided with a room
senses.example: The board will meet on Friday.

senses.definition: to get onto a vehicle, or live somewhere while receiving meals
senses.example: We boarded the train at noon.

senses.definition: to look for someone or something, or try to obtain it
senses.example: She is seeking a new job.

senses.definition: for each unit of time, money, or quantity, or according to an instruction
senses.example: The train travels at 100 kilometres per hour.

senses.definition: a topic of discussion, a school course, a person or thing being studied, or the main part of a sentence
senses.example: Maths was her favourite subject at school.

senses.definition: likely to experience something or depending on a condition
senses.example: The trip is subject to the weather.

senses.definition: to cause someone to experience something unpleasant
senses.example: They subjected the animals to loud noise.
senses.note: 名词重音在前 /ˈsʌbdʒɪkt/；动词重音在后 /səbˈdʒekt/。

senses.zh: 官员；警官；军官；高级职员
senses.definition: a person with an official position in government, police, the military, or an organization
senses.example: A police officer helped us cross the road.

senses.zh: 私人的；私有的；非公开的；私立的
senses.definition: belonging to one person or group, not open to everyone, or not run by the state
senses.example: This is a private conversation.

senses.definition: a soldier of the lowest rank in an army
senses.example: The private reported to the officer.
senses.note: 名词“列兵”仅用于军事语境；日常重点是形容词“私人、私立”。

senses.definition: time spent relaxing, what remains, or something used to support an object
senses.example: You need a good rest after the trip.

senses.definition: to stop working for a while or place something on a surface
senses.example: Let's rest for a few minutes.

senses.definition: to handle a situation, buy or sell, or give cards to players
senses.example: We need to deal with this problem today.

senses.zh: 交易；协议；待遇；很大数量
senses.definition: an agreement in business, a particular way of treating someone, or a large amount
senses.example: They made a deal to share the costs.

senses.definition: how well a person or machine works, or an act of performing for an audience
senses.example: Her performance in the exam improved.

senses.zh: 打架；战斗；反对；努力争取
senses.definition: to use force against someone, oppose a problem, or struggle to achieve something
senses.example: They fought to protect the forest.

senses.definition: an act of using force, a serious disagreement, or an effort to stop a problem
senses.example: The children had a fight over a toy.

senses.definition: to send something through the air with your hand, or cause something to enter a new state suddenly
senses.example: Please throw the ball to me.

senses.definition: an act of sending something through the air with your hand, or how far it travels
senses.example: That was a good throw.

senses.definition: the highest part of something, an upper garment, or the highest rank
senses.example: We climbed to the top of the hill.

senses.zh: 最上面的；最好的；首要的
senses.definition: highest in position, rank, or importance
senses.example: She is one of the top students.

senses.definition: to be higher than something else, exceed it, or reach the top
senses.example: The tower tops every other building nearby.

senses.definition: at a fast speed or after only a short time
senses.example: She quickly found the right page.

senses.definition: by or beyond a place, time, or amount
senses.example: We walked past the library.

senses.definition: belonging to a time before now
senses.example: She has worked there for the past year.

senses.definition: the time before now or the events of that time
senses.example: We cannot change the past.

senses.definition: from one side to another or beyond a point
senses.example: A car drove past.

senses.definition: something a person wants to achieve, the frame to score through, or a score in a sport
senses.example: Her goal is to run five kilometres.

senses.definition: a piece of furniture for sleeping, a planted area, or the bottom of a river
senses.example: The child went to bed early.

senses.definition: an arrangement, an instruction, a request to buy something, or a controlled state
senses.example: The books are in alphabetical order.

senses.definition: to tell someone to do something, request goods or food, or arrange things
senses.example: We ordered lunch online.

senses.definition: a person who writes a book, report, or other work
senses.example: The author signed her new book.

senses.definition: to write or create a book, report, or other work
senses.example: She authored several articles on education.

senses.definition: to make a space full, write information in a form, or meet a need
senses.example: Please fill the glass with water.

senses.definition: as much of something as you want or need
senses.example: The children ate their fill.
senses.note: 名词常见于 eat your fill、have your fill 等固定短语。

senses.definition: to speak for someone, stand for an idea, or show something in a particular way
senses.example: She represents her school at the event.

senses.definition: the main thing receiving attention, a clear point in an image, or the distance for clear imaging
senses.example: The focus of the lesson was speaking.

senses.definition: to give attention to one thing or make an image clear
senses.example: Please focus on the question.

senses.zh: 外国的；外来的；不熟悉的
senses.definition: from another country or not familiar in a particular setting
senses.example: She is learning a foreign language.

senses.definition: to fall, let something fall, become lower, or stop doing something
senses.example: The temperature dropped overnight.

senses.definition: a small amount of liquid, a little of something, or a fall in level
senses.example: Add a drop of water to the paint.

senses.definition: the red liquid moving through a person's or animal's body, or family origin in formal use
senses.example: The nurse took a sample of blood.

senses.definition: on something, immediately after an event, or depending on something
senses.example: Upon arrival, please call me.
senses.note: upon 比 on 更正式；许多用法出现在固定短语中。

senses.zh: 机构；代理公司；经纪机构
senses.definition: an organization that provides a service or acts for other people
senses.example: She works for a travel agency.

senses.definition: to use force to move something away, encourage an action, or try hard to achieve it
senses.example: Push the door gently to open it.

senses.definition: an act of moving something with force or a strong effort to achieve something
senses.example: Give the door a firm push.

senses.definition: the living world and its processes, or the basic character of a person or thing
senses.example: The children enjoy spending time in nature.

senses.definition: the appearance something has because of light, or a substance used to change that appearance
senses.example: What color is your new bike?
senses.note: 美式拼写 color；英式通常写 colour。

senses.zh: 给…着色；使带有色彩；影响
senses.definition: to add color to something or influence the way it is seen
senses.example: She colored the picture with pencils.
senses.note: 美式拼写 color；英式通常写 colour。

senses.definition: not long ago
senses.example: I saw her recently at the library.

senses.definition: a place that sells goods, or a supply kept for future use
senses.example: I bought milk at the store.

senses.definition: to keep something for use later
senses.example: Store the medicine in a cool place.

senses.definition: to make something smaller, lower, or less, or cause it to be in a worse state
senses.example: We need to reduce waste at home.

senses.definition: something you hear, or the way a voice or recording is heard
senses.example: I heard a strange sound outside.

senses.definition: to seem a particular way when heard, or make a noise
senses.example: That sounds like a good idea.

senses.definition: healthy or working well, or based on good judgment
senses.example: The plan is based on sound advice.
senses.note: sound asleep 意为“睡得很熟”，不要逐字译成“声音睡着”。

senses.definition: a short written message, a record made to remember something, or a musical sound
senses.example: I wrote a note to remind myself.

senses.definition: to notice something, write it down, or mention it
senses.example: Please note the time of the meeting.

senses.zh: 好的；可以的；优质的；细的
senses.definition: satisfactory or very good, or very thin and small
senses.example: I'm fine, thank you.

senses.definition: in a satisfactory way
senses.example: The new phone works fine.

senses.definition: money paid as punishment for breaking a rule or law
senses.example: He had to pay a fine for parking there.

senses.definition: to make someone pay money as punishment for breaking a rule
senses.example: The police fined him for speeding.

evidence.note: Cambridge lists common adjective, adverb, noun, and verb senses.

senses.definition: at a short distance from a place, person, or time
senses.example: We live near the school.

senses.definition: not far away in distance, time, or degree
senses.example: The nearest shop is five minutes away.

senses.definition: at a short distance away or almost at a point
senses.example: Come nearer so I can hear you.

senses.definition: the act of changing position, or a group of people working for a common aim
senses.example: I saw movement behind the curtain.

senses.definition: one side of a sheet in a book or an area of information on a website
senses.example: Please turn to page ten.

senses.definition: to call someone over a public speaker or message system, or leaf through a book
senses.example: The nurse paged the doctor.
senses.note: 动词 page 多见于医院呼叫或翻书语境。

senses.definition: to go into a place, put information into a system, or join a competition
senses.example: Enter your name in the form.

senses.definition: happening often, shared by several people, or not unusual
senses.example: This is a common mistake for learners.

senses.definition: an open area of land that local people may use
senses.example: The children played on the village common.
senses.note: 名词只在“公共草地”等特定语境使用；先记形容词。

senses.definition: to use or have something with someone else, or tell others about it
senses.example: We share the housework equally.

senses.definition: one part of an amount or business owned by someone
senses.example: She bought shares in the company.

senses.definition: having little money, low in quality, or deserving sympathy
senses.example: The roads are in poor condition.

senses.definition: existing in nature rather than made by people, or happening without effort
senses.example: The juice contains only natural ingredients.

senses.definition: a competition to see who is fastest, or a group of people once classified by shared physical features
senses.example: She won the race by two seconds.

senses.definition: to compete in speed or move very quickly
senses.example: The children raced across the field.

senses.definition: a feeling of worry, an interest in someone, or an important matter
senses.example: Her main concern is the children's safety.

senses.definition: to make someone worried or be about or affect them
senses.example: The news concerns everyone in the town.

senses.zh: 系列；连续的一组；系列节目
senses.definition: a group of connected things, events, books, or television programmes
senses.example: We watched the first episode of the series.
senses.note: 单复数同形：one series、two series。

senses.zh: 重要的；显著的；有意义的
senses.definition: large or important enough to be noticed, or having a special meaning
senses.example: The change made a significant difference.

senses.definition: almost the same but not exactly the same
senses.example: The two pictures look similar.

senses.zh: 热的；烫的；辛辣的；热门的
senses.definition: having a high temperature, tasting spicy, or attracting much interest
senses.example: The soup is too hot to eat.

senses.definition: a system of words used by a group of people, or a particular way of speaking
senses.example: English is not her first language.

senses.definition: in most situations or most of the time
senses.example: We usually eat dinner at seven.

senses.definition: an answer or reaction to something that happens or is said
senses.example: She sent a quick response to my email.

senses.definition: no longer alive, working, or active
senses.example: The phone is dead because its battery is empty.

senses.definition: completely or extremely in a few fixed expressions
senses.example: I was dead tired after the trip.
senses.note: 副词义多用于口语固定搭配。

senses.definition: to move upwards, get out of a sitting position, or become greater
senses.example: Prices rose again this month.

senses.definition: an increase in level, number, or value
senses.example: There was a rise in the cost of food.

senses.definition: a living thing that can move and eat plants or other animals
senses.example: The elephant is a large animal.

senses.definition: relating to animals or physical instincts
senses.example: The clinic studies animal behaviour.

senses.definition: one of the things that affects a result, or a number that divides another number exactly
senses.example: Cost is an important factor in our decision.

senses.definition: to include something in a calculation or express a number as factors
senses.example: We factored travel costs into the budget.

senses.definition: a period of ten years
senses.example: The town has changed a lot over the past decade.

senses.definition: television as a system, its programmes, or a television set
senses.example: We watched a nature programme on TV.

removedPos.word: 旧词性 word 是占位标签，不是实际词性；TV 在这些用法中作名词。

senses.definition: a piece of writing, a grammar word such as a or the, or an item
senses.example: I read an article about sleep.

senses.zh: 射击；拍摄；投篮；迅速移动
senses.definition: to fire a weapon, make a film or photo, send a ball towards a goal, or move suddenly
senses.example: They shot a short film at school.

senses.definition: new plant growth or an organized time to take photographs or film
senses.example: The first green shoots appeared in spring.

evidence.note: Cambridge lists plant growth and photo/film shoot as noun senses.

senses.definition: the direction where the sun rises, or the eastern part of a place
senses.example: The sun rises in the east.

senses.definition: located towards the eastern part of a place
senses.example: They live on the east side of town.

senses.definition: towards or in the eastern direction
senses.example: We travelled east for two days.

senses.definition: the number 7
senses.example: There are seven days in a week.

senses.definition: to keep someone safe, use less of something, store information, or put money aside
senses.example: Please save your work before closing the file.

senses.zh: 艺术家；画家；表演艺术工作者
senses.definition: a person who creates visual art, or a person whose work is in a creative art
senses.example: The artist painted a picture of the river.

senses.zh: 场景；现场；戏剧或电影中的一场
senses.definition: a place where something happens, or one part of a play or film
senses.example: The final scene of the film made us laugh.

senses.definition: the number 8
senses.example: The class begins at eight.

senses.definition: goods kept for sale, a supply for later use, a share of a company, or liquid used in cooking
senses.example: The shop has this book in stock.

senses.definition: to keep goods available for sale or fill a place with supplies
senses.example: The shop stocks several kinds of tea.

senses.definition: kept ready for use or repeated so often that it is not original
senses.example: That was his stock answer to every question.

evidence.note: Learner dictionary lists stock inventory, shares, cooking liquid and adjective.

senses.definition: the series of jobs a person has during their working life, or their progress in one field
senses.example: She began her career as a teacher.

senses.definition: used to say that something happened although another fact could have prevented it
senses.example: We went for a walk despite the rain.
senses.note: despite 后接名词或 -ing；不要写 despite of。

senses.zh: 中心的；中央的；最重要的
senses.definition: in the middle of a place or very important to an idea or activity
senses.example: The library is in a central location.

senses.definition: for this reason, or in the way just described
senses.example: The bus was late, so we missed the start; thus we joined halfway through.
senses.note: thus 比 so 更正式，常见于书面语。

senses.definition: medical care, the way a person is dealt with, or a process used on a material
senses.example: She received treatment for her injury.

senses.definition: on the other side of a place, further than a limit, or after a time
senses.example: The park is beyond the bridge.

senses.definition: further away or at a later point
senses.example: The valley and beyond were covered in snow.

senses.definition: feeling pleasure or satisfaction
senses.example: She was happy to hear the good news.

senses.definition: in a precise way or to the exact degree stated
senses.example: The train arrived at exactly six.

senses.definition: to keep someone or something safe from harm or damage
senses.example: Wear a hat to protect your head from the sun.

senses.definition: a way of dealing with something, the act of getting nearer, or a path leading to a place
senses.example: We need a different approach to this problem.

senses.definition: to move nearer, begin to deal with a problem, or contact someone with a request
senses.example: How should we approach this task?

evidence.note: Cambridge lists noun method/arrival and verb come near/deal with/contact.

senses.definition: something someone says knowing it is not true
senses.example: He told a lie about where he had been.

senses.definition: to rest flat, be in a particular place, or say something untrue to deceive
senses.example: The cat likes to lie in the sun.
senses.note: “躺”过去式 lay、过去分词 lain；“说谎”过去式和过去分词均为 lied。例：He lied to me。不要与及物动词 lay（放下）混淆。

evidence.note: Cambridge distinguishes irregular lie = recline from regular lie = say falsehood.
Grammar reference separates lay and lie forms.

senses.definition: how big something is, or the measurement used to describe it
senses.example: What size shoes do you wear?

senses.definition: to measure something or make it a particular size
senses.example: They sized the shoes for each child.

senses.definition: an animal often kept as a pet and known for barking
senses.example: Our dog loves running in the park.

senses.definition: to follow someone persistently or continue causing them trouble
senses.example: The problem dogged the team for months.
senses.note: 动词义多用于书面语；日常先记名词“狗”。

senses.definition: money saved or collected for a particular purpose
senses.example: The school set up a fund for new books.

senses.definition: to provide money for a project or activity
senses.example: The charity funds local schools.

senses.definition: important or dangerous, careful in purpose, or not joking
senses.example: The storm caused serious damage.

senses.definition: to happen, exist in a place, or come into someone's mind
senses.example: The accident occurred last night.

senses.definition: organizations and methods that provide news and entertainment to many people
senses.example: The story received a lot of media attention.
senses.note: media 原是 medium 的复数；表示大众媒体时既见复数也见集合名词用法。

senses.zh: 准备好的；愿意的；现成的
senses.definition: prepared for something, willing to act, or available for immediate use
senses.example: Dinner is ready.

senses.definition: to prepare something for use or an event
senses.example: They readied the room for the guests.
senses.note: 动词 ready 较少见，日常常说 prepare 或 get ready。

senses.definition: a mark or notice giving information, evidence that something exists, or a gesture with meaning
senses.example: The sign says the park closes at six.

senses.definition: to write your name to show agreement, or communicate with a gesture
senses.example: Please sign your name here.

senses.definition: an idea in your mind or the act of thinking
senses.example: That's an interesting thought.

senses.zh: 想；认为；以为（think 的过去式）
senses.definition: the past form of think, used when you had an idea or opinion earlier
senses.example: I thought the meeting started at nine.
senses.note: thought 是 think 的过去式和过去分词；不是现在时原形。

senses.definition: a series of names or things written one after another
senses.example: I made a list of things to buy.

senses.definition: to write or name things one after another
senses.example: Please list three reasons for your choice.

senses.definition: one person or thing considered separately from a group
senses.example: Each individual has different needs.

senses.definition: relating to one person or thing rather than to a group
senses.example: We discussed each individual's progress.

evidence.note: Cambridge lists both noun and adjective.
